props.title: Look Back in Anger
props.initialSlug: Angry young man rages against British society

sections.content: **Look Back in Anger** (1959) launched Britain's "angry young men" movement onto the screen, with Richard Burton's explosive performance as Jimmy Porter defining working-class rage for a generation. Adapted from John Osborne's groundbreaking 1956 play, the film captured the simmering frustration of post-war British youth trapped by rigid class structures. Director Tony Richardson, who would later spearhead the British New Wave with The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (1962), brings raw emotional authenticity that influenced Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (1960) and **This Sporting Life** (1963).

sections.content: The kitchen sink realism movement that **Look Back in Anger** helped launch transformed British cinema. Directors like Karel Reisz, Lindsay Anderson, and Tony Richardson stripped away Hollywood glamour to show working-class life with unprecedented honesty. **A Taste of Honey** (1961) tackled teenage pregnancy and homosexuality, while **This Sporting Life** (1963) exposed the brutality beneath professional rugby through Richard Harris's tortured performance.

Burton's Jimmy Porter became the prototype for a new kind of British anti-hero - educated but trapped in his class, articulate but unable to change his circumstances. This character type influenced performances from Albert Finney in Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (1960) to Malcolm McDowell in **If....** (1968), establishing a tradition of rebellion that would later surface in punk cinema like **Quadrophenia** (1979). SUBHEAD: Impact on British Social Realism

sections.content: The film's visual style - cramped interiors, documentary-like street scenes, emphasis on regional accents and locations - created a template for British social realism that continues through directors like Ken Loach (**Kes** [1969], **Poor Cow** [1967]) and Mike Leigh (**Naked** [1993], **Secrets & Lies** [1996]). The marriage between theatrical intensity and cinematic naturalism influenced later kitchen sink dramas like **Nil By Mouth** (1997) and **This Is England** (2006).
